newsitem.title: LEBANON: Banque Audi shares start trading on Beirut market.
newsitem.headline: Banque Audi shares start trading on Beirut market.

text.p: The start of trading in shares of Banque Audi, one of Lebanon's most active banks, on the Beirut Stock Exchange (BSE) on Monday offers hope that new bank listings will pump new blood into the lacklustre market, dealers said.
Audi, traded at $15 on turnover of 10,000 shares, was the second bank to list on the exchange following the December 30 debut of Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce (BLC).
At least one other leading Beirut bank, Byblos Bank, is expected to list its shares soon.
Dealers say they expect the bank shares to boost the bourse which has been lacklustre since it reopened in January 1996 after a 13-year shutdown due to Lebanon's 1975-90 civil war.

"There has been an increase in turnover in the market (after the bank listings). This brings in more money and liquidity will rise. It is good news," Alain Balian, deputy manager structured finance at Lebanon Invest finance house, told Reuters.
"Banks are more transparent than other companies and that brings in more investors," he added.
"There was demand for 60,000 to 70,000 Audi shares but offer was 10,000," a dealer said.

The bank listings were carried out under a law passed last year allowing Lebanese commercial banks to list and trade 30 percent of their shares on the Beirut Stock Exchange without prior permission from the central bank.
Audi offered all its 4,158,000 C shares -- or 30 percent of its total number of shares -- for trading on BSE. The bank shares have a nominal value of 2,000 Lebanese pounds ($1.29).
BLC has been a star performer since its shares began trading at $11.25 three weeks ago. On Monday, they were unchanged from Friday's $12.375 on trade of 1,500 shares.
BLC, Audi and Byblos are among Beirut's most active banks. All have in the past 17 months raised capital through public or private share issues on local and international markets.
Dealers said Banque Audi GDRs -- a $34 million issue made in 1995 to international investors -- were trading at $15-$15.50 on the Luxembourg bourse on Monday, up from Friday's $14-$14.50.
"Since the shares opened at $15 today, we expected the GDRs to go up today," one dealer said.
Audi launched a heavily oversubscribed $100 million Eurobond in October lead-managed by Merrill Lynch International.

It is the third Lebanese bank ranked by capital, and in 1995 was also third among Beirut's 82 banks in terms of deposits. Its profits were 14 billion Lebanese pounds in the first half of 1996 against 20 billion for the whole of 1995.

Also on the BSE, Solidere A shares rose to $10.5 from Friday's record low of $10.25 and B shares fell to $11.125 from Friday's $11.25. Turnover in Solidere was 33,446 from Friday's 33,105 and value was $358,321.5 from $310,614.75.
There was no trade in the four other listed firms: Ciments Libanais, Ciments Blancs, Eternit and Uniceramic.
